auto_update._doc_max_installs_per_pass: Most install sessions ONE unattended background pass may open. A background pass cannot show the system install dialog (Android 10+ blocks background activity starts), so each install it starts leaves a tap-to-install notification holding a PackageInstaller session until the user answers it. Unbounded, one pass over the 40-entry fleet opens 40 and the installer hits Android's 50-session cap - 'Too many active sessions for UID'. The remainder is picked up by the next pass. User-initiated 'Update all' is NOT capped: it runs in the foreground where the dialog appears and sessions resolve at once.

fleet_endpoints._doc: #1093 THE fleet endpoint declaration, declared once (#1090 declared the mail part of it as mail_endpoints). Every fleet service Cloud Account talks to or shows has up to two endpoints, taken from the service's own fleet declaration in cloud-u-containers (`source`): mesh_dns / mesh_port / mesh_scheme = containers.app.dns / .port / .protocol, public_domain = proxy.domain. libs:account reads this for four things: (1) Account's own transport (libs:fleet-endpoints: mesh first with a short probe, then the public URL with the fleet bearer, cached, re-probed on a network change), (2) Connect > Status > Endpoints, (3) the `fleet_endpoints` accountdata method that publishes the pairs to the other apps, and (4) the `mail_endpoints` method, which takes the kind=mail services (Cloud Mail). A service that lives under a PATH of a shared host says public_path (and mesh_path when the mesh side differs) and route_paths (the part of it that may be routed). The vault is declared with `auth: mtls`: its public URL (vault.diegonmarcos.com) is reached from a mesh source or with the per-device mTLS client certificate, it is never rewritten onto a mesh name by the router and never receives the bearer. `auth` is bearer (default) | mtls | sso (Authelia: auth.diegonmarcos.com with its sso./account. `aliases`); `ssh_hosts` lists the git ssh host entries. A service with no public_domain is mesh-only (no public route is declared, or the public name is WG-only) and must say policy mesh_only; the bearer is never declared here: it is the vault's fleet.bearer, granted per package in Secrets and sent on the exact public origin only. policy is the default: mesh_first (try the mesh, fall back to public + bearer), mesh_only, public_only. health is the path Status asks for. Every mesh endpoint is plain http (`<container>.mesh.diegonmarcos.com` is WireGuard-only, WG encrypts) and every public URL https; each app's network_security_config.xml gets its cleartext mesh entries GENERATED from this list (1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-fleet-nsc.py, data 1_cicd/src/data/fleet-nsc.json, held by FleetHostGuardTest), never hand-listed.

services._doc: #1162 The fleet agent gateway (my-ai-api, service cloud-agi-goose, WireGuard-only) libs:ai's AiGatewayBackend talks to; Cloud SuperIntel lists it in fleet-nsc.json so its cleartext entry is generated like every other mesh host.

#1179 The fleet embeddings + rerank + PDF text server (Infinity, CPU, WireGuard-only on oci-apps): POST /embeddings (OpenAI-compatible, BAAI/bge-m3), POST /rerank (BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3), POST /pdf (raw application/pdf body, JSON {pages, text}), GET /models. Cloud SuperIntel Notebook retrieval and Cloud Tools Retrieval steps bake this base URL (fleetMeshUrl('embeddings-api')) and fall back to on-phone BM25 when it does not answer. Direct dial on the mesh (Hickory row embeddings-api -> 10.0.0.6), so mesh_only: no public route exists.

#1179 The fleet Ollama: the Ollama-compatible API of my-ai-api (BRIDGE_OLLAMA_PORT 12436, bound on oci-apps' WireGuard address 10.0.0.6; GET /api/tags and /v1/models; no /api/ps). Same service and mesh name as the ai-gateway entry, on its Ollama port; Cloud Tools' Store location Fleet Ollama bakes this base URL (fleetMeshUrl('ollama')). Mesh-only.

The mesh endpoint is the fleet's convention: the mesh name is WireGuard-only and WG already encrypts, so it is plain HTTP on the service's mesh-only port (2080 -> Stalwart's HTTP listener, bound on wg0 and wg-public like its other mesh ports; cloud-u-containers user-comm_tools-stalwart extra_ports must map it). Until that listener is shipped the mesh probe fails and Mail runs on the public URL with the bearer (the verdict is cached), so nothing breaks. The public URL stays https.

The fleet's mesh mirror of release assets (#837): the Store and the updater download through it (their own MeshMirror order). Mesh-only, declared here so its cleartext entry is generated like every other mesh host.
Only the health probe is routed: a sign-in is a browser or cookie flow bound to the auth host (Authelia refuses a session on another host name), so every other path stays on the public URL.

#1100 addressing rule: the public name is {container}.diegonmarcos.com (no api.* host, no /pub path of a shared host). mesh_path empty. route_paths is the part a direct mesh call may reach: /health, /ready and /analytics/* are the declared public_paths; the config artifact and profile connect are answered only behind the gate and stay on the public URL. The mesh leg answers once #1100 publishes the container on the mesh; until then a mesh probe fails fast and the public URL + bearer is used.

Capital-Stack-FinTerminal's primary data source (Cloud-Fincept / fin_api): the FinceptTerminal backend on oci-apps (container capital-stack-finterminal-api, containers.app.port 8340). Its retired public host answers 302 to sign-in (#1104) and api.diegonmarcos.com/fin-api is wg_only, so it is MESH-ONLY: fin-api.mesh.diegonmarcos.com:8340 (10.0.0.6), GET /health, /api/v1/info, /api/v1/topics, /api/v1/topics/{topic}/peek.

#1104 addressing: public c3-pvt.diegonmarcos.com/c3-infra-api (fleet bearer; the per-container public hosts are on hold), mesh c3-infra-api.mesh.diegonmarcos.com. Only its declared paths are routed over the mesh (the per-app crash/log route /apk/{name}/logs and /containers/{name}/logs, crash and log events, public logs); the rest answers behind the gate only. The mesh leg answers once #1100 publishes the container on the mesh; until then the public URL + bearer is used.

#1100 addressing rule: public {container}.diegonmarcos.com behind the fleet bearer (no api.* host, no /news prefix); mesh news-gdelt.mesh.diegonmarcos.com:3019 (the name resolves on the mesh; the port is not published yet, so until #1100 publishes it the public URL + bearer is used). libs:news reads its default API base from this entry (BuildConfig.NEWS_API_BASE) and sends its calls over the seam. Only the read endpoints are routed.

#1184 The fleet's PUBLIC code index (octocode semantic search + GraphRAG over the public repos), streamable-HTTP MCP at /mcp: containers.app (port 3105, mesh dns cloud-cgc-pub-mcp.mesh.diegonmarcos.com) and the hub route mcp.diegonmarcos.com/cloud-cgc-pub-mcp. Cloud Research's Cloud-CGC reads it; mesh first, then the public route with the fleet bearer.

#1184 The PRIVATE surface of the same image (containers.pvt, CGC_SURFACE=pvt, port 3107, cloud-data and cloud-me-pvt-my-ai): WireGuard-only, so mesh_only and no public address (its hub route is wg_only). Cloud Research's Me-CGC reads it behind the Cloud Account sign-in. Its index is not built yet (the deploy keys for the private repositories are missing), and the page says what the service answers.

wg_only: languagetool.diegonmarcos.com answers on the mesh alone (a remote_ip gate), so it is no second endpoint and the policy is mesh_only: the Keyboard's grammar check uses the mesh endpoint and fails as unreachable off the mesh.
No public_domain: the broker's public leg is a path under auth.diegonmarcos.com that Authelia's edge fronts, not an endpoint of its own. Its google instance (4180) stands for the broker here.

The fleet token engine behind Data > Secrets > Tokens: owner-only (the engine checks the phone's fleet bearer), mesh first, then the private tier c3-pvt.diegonmarcos.com/tokens-api (#1104) behind the shared gate.

The owner's private data (cloud-me-* repos), incl. the Autocomplete rows GET /me/autocomplete (#1103): mesh first, then the private tier c3-pvt.diegonmarcos.com/cloud-me-api (#1104) behind the shared gate. The service also verifies the Authelia bearer itself.

Cloud Vault's server (Vaultwarden). Private: the mesh name, no credential. Public fallback: vault.diegonmarcos.com behind the per-device mTLS client certificate (`verify_if_given`, no bearer and no token in a URL: the Bitwarden client sends none). `auth: mtls` keeps the fleet bearer off this host and keeps the router from rewriting it onto the mesh; Cloud Vault itself tries the mesh, then the public URL with its certificate.

account._doc: Cloud Account redesign, task 2 (a0_docs/eng-specs/cloud-account-redesign.md sections 2, 5, 6). Read by libs:account's build.gradle into BuildConfig.UI_ACCOUNT_B64 (ForgeClient.Decl). forges: where the vault lives, each written through its contents API; auth 'bearer' sends `Authorization: Bearer <t>` (GitHub), 'token' sends `Authorization: token <t>` (Gitea). A forge's token is read from AccountVault Connections at forge.<id>.token, the primary forge id at forge.primary (default: the first forge with a repo). vault: the branch, the folder the app writes per-device profiles to (devices/<id>.json, DEFAULT.json; never an emit.py input), and the generated secrets file the connect fetch keeps reading.

forges._doc_repo: null on purpose: the vault repo is NOT mirrored to Gitea (cloud-u-containers infra-dat_gitea build.json mirror_policy.exclude lists cloud-vault and cloud-me-pvt-vault), so no owner/repo path exists there. The owner declares it once a private Gitea repo for the vault exists; until then this forge is skipped (ForgeClient refuses a forge without a repo).

runbook._doc: Setup runbook (spec section 4.6): the eight step ids IN ORDER, read by libs:account SetupRunbook from BuildConfig.UI_ACCOUNT_B64. Removing an id disables that step by declaration. Implemented so far: shell (embedded adb pairing + WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS self-grant), store (install Cloud Store from the fleet release over the shell channel). The others answer TODO until their slot lands.

connect._doc: Account ▸ connect (spec 4.2): the forge ways are ui.account.forges[].ways; this adds the offline way. libs:account ConnectWays.ways() reads both and dispatches every pill on its kind (ConnectWays.handler).

perms._doc: Setup ▸ perms (spec 4.9): the shell verb table libs:account PermsPlan reads from BuildConfig.UI_ACCOUNT_B64 (nothing in Kotlin names a verb). Each verb is a template run over the uid-2000 shell channel; {pkg} {perm} {op} {component} {role} are substituted only after a strict name check. 'PackageVerifier' is not a shell line: it names the existing lib object that writes the Play Protect Settings.Global keys. needs_user: the kinds the shell cannot grant (device admin, accessibility) and the Settings action each row opens. appops: shell op name -> the AppOpsManager opstr read back and the manifest permission (or service permission) that makes an app list the row; NOTIFICATION_LISTENER is recorded with the app ops in the profile. roles: short name -> role id.

configs_pages._doc: Configs > General and Configs > About (libs:ui-nav-bars fleetconfigs, rule 1_cicd/src/data/configs-pages.json, #1352 v2). general.sections: the anchors of the one General page, in order (perms, battery, storage, notifications, ui, language are required; app opens this app's own Configs; update is added after perms by default). about: the hand-written part of the extensive About: tagline, description, features, screens, guide, privacy, backends (ids of ac_cloud-account/build.json::fleet_endpoints, resolved to mesh URLs at build time), related fleet apps, credits for a fork. Permissions, data stores, crash/analytics libs, name, icon, version, build sha and date, repo, licence, origin, crash sink, debug API and changelog are derived, never typed here.

about.tagline: Turns an empty phone into your phone, and keeps it so
about.description: Cloud Account is the fleet's identity and setup app. It holds the owner's account and its sign-in ways, the per-device profile that is backed up to and restored from the private vault repository, the fleet secrets and tokens every other app reads through it, and the setup that turns a freshly installed phone into the owner's phone. It exists so that no app keeps its own copy of a secret, and so a new or reset phone is back to normal in minutes rather than an afternoon.
features: Configs for Android, desktop and C3

screens.name: Activity
screens.what: The log of what changed and when.

guide: Sign in once on Connect; every fleet app then reads its token from here.
Use Data ▸ Backups to back up this phone's profile to the vault.
On a new phone, restore the profile from Data, then let Cloud Store install the fleet.
Check Activity when something changed and you do not know why.
about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback; nothing leaves the device unless you share it. It talks only to the fleet services listed below, over the private mesh first.

The password vault behind the account's secrets.
Uses the vault's passwords for autofill.

perms._doc: #1360 every grant this app needs, by libs:perms catalogue id (needs), and the fleet apps that do work for it with the grants THEY must hold (helpers). The ONE declaration: generated into assets/app-perms.json (cloud-android-perms-guard.py --write), drawn by Configs > General > Perms (libs:perms AppPermsSection) with live state, Grant / Open and Grant all, asked at first run (first_run), and reported as 'Missing permission X - Grant' when an operation fails (PermsGate). perms-guard fails when code uses a gated API or another app's engine that is not declared here, or when the manifest and this list disagree.
